what_worked: Popularity-vs-profitability scatter and growth-vs-subscriber quartile comparison deliver genuinely contrarian, data-grounded arguments.
fix_next: Label every chart axis with actual category/metric names—three charts use only numeric indices, crippling readability and verifiability.
verdict: Strong narrative arc undermined by mislabeled charts and several factual errors in category claims.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: Top-3 stated as AI/SaaS/Education but by frozen reference Marketing ($1.32M) and E-commerce ($1.11M) both outrank SaaS ($703K) and Education ($524K); 49.8% share doesn't match those three. Slide 4/5/9: AI median stated as $446 but reference gives $503. Slide 2: '$334M combined all-time revenue' is unverifiable and inconsistent with the $15.6M monthly snapshot. Slide 3: '30.8% AI share of revenue' doesn't reconcile with reference AI total ($2.36M of ~$7.4M categorized ≈ 32%, close but denominator unclear given 274 missing categories). Slide 9: AI median repeated as $446.

evidence.insight: Crowding-vs-median scatter (slide 4), subscriber-quartile staircase vs flat growth quartiles (slide 7), freemium median gap, and vanity-growth anecdote all challenge conventional wisdom with dataset-specific evidence. Small-n caveat on hidden gems (n=5–7) limits actionability.
evidence.narrative: Clean arc: long-tail framing → concentration → crowding paradox → predictive signals → surprising patterns → recommendations → closing thesis. Each slide advances the argument. Thesis stated early (slide 2) and landed cleanly (slide 10).
evidence.framing: Audience (founders/investors) stated on slide 1; dataset scope and freeze date noted. However, no mention of 274 missing categories or 241 missing countries, which materially affect category-level claims. No limitations slide. The $334M all-time figure appears without reconciliation.
evidence.accuracy: Top-3 category composition is wrong—Marketing and E-commerce outrank SaaS and Education by total revenue. AI median is $503 not $446. The 49.8% share doesn't match the stated AI/SaaS/Education grouping against reference totals. Spearman correlations on slide 6 are plausible but unverifiable. Freemium/paid comparison is interesting but outside reference data.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/gold palette, clean typography, effective callout boxes. But slides 3, 5, and 6 use numeric-only y-axis labels (1–8, 1–5) instead of category or metric names, making charts unreadable without guessing. Scatter plot on slide 4 is well-executed with color coding. Template is polished but repeated unlabeled axes are a serious legibility flaw.
evidence.ai_slop: Consulting-style phrasing ('executive briefing,' 'hidden gems,' 'gold rush') is present but not excessive. Four-card layouts on slides 2 and 8 are template-ish but populated with specific data points. Not egregious.

change_reason: Lowered framing by 0.5 (no missingness disclosure is more serious given category-dependent claims) and visual by 0.5 (three charts with unlabeled axes is a recurring legibility failure, not a one-off). Other scores confirmed as appropriate.
